sources.entry: Haven - Private blogging system with markdown editing and built in RSS reader. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Ruby

summary.one_liner: Haven is a private, invite-only blogging application built with Ruby on Rails, with markdown editing, private RSS feeds, and a built-in RSS reader for following friends' blogs.
summary.what_it_does: Haven lets you write and publish blog posts using markdown with live preview, and manage users and blog customization through a built-in web interface. There is no self-signup; the owner creates accounts for the people they want to share with. Each blog gets private RSS feeds so friends can follow it, and a built-in RSS reader lets users follow other blogs and other Havens. Media support covers images, videos, and audio, and images are downscaled to reduce page load size. Custom CSS and fonts can be added. The README states it uses no JavaScript frameworks and has no ads or trackers.
use_cases: Sharing a private blog with friends and family
Writing markdown posts with live preview
Following friends' blogs via RSS in one place
Running an invite-only blog without spam signups
Self-hosting a blog on Docker or AWS
how_to_run: git clone the haven repository and cd into haven
Edit HAVEN_USER_EMAIL and HAVEN_USER_PASS in docker-compose.yml (optional)
notable: Private, invite-only accounts with no public self-signup
Built-in RSS reader for following other blogs and Havens
Private RSS feeds for friends to follow your posts
Markdown editor with live preview and image downscaling for low bandwidth
Multiple deployment paths including Docker, AWS scripts, and hosted options
caveats: The README says it is for personal sharing, not commercial blogs; it recommends WordPress or Ghost for company blogs
The Heroku install is meant for experimentation; uploaded images may disappear within 24 hours and Heroku's free tier is being eliminated (about $16/month expected)
AWS deployment takes around 20 minutes and requires an AWS account, Route 53 domain, and credentials
